title: Terminal booking states, and the wait-list channel disabled until a wait-list exists

terminal_states.rule: completed and cancelled are BOTH terminal. A cancelled booking cannot be reassigned - the customer creates a new booking. A completed booking cannot return to reassignment_needed. Booking, cancellation, payment, refund and audit history are preserved. An in-progress service must NOT be auto-cancelled or regressed because a provider document later expires or is rejected; the work stays intact and Operations gets a case.
terminal_states.what_already_existed: The guards themselves were closed earlier in this audit, in lib/sitting-lifecycle.ts, lib/walking-lifecycle.ts, lib/boarding-stay-lifecycle.ts and lib/taxi-lifecycle.ts, and lib/provider-assignment-eligibility.ts already opens cases rather than cancelling work.
terminal_states.what_was_missing: EXECUTABLE PROOF for two of the four verticals and for the in-progress half. tests/ptja-w1-leftover-regressions.test.mjs covers Sitting and Walking only. Boarding had the guard with no test, and Pet Taxi - the vertical that WROTE the rule - had no test of it either. Per the business's instruction that nothing closes on source inspection, that gap is now filled.
terminal_states.honest_note: These cases are GREEN on arrival rather than red-first, because the production behaviour was already correct. Each is sabotage-verified instead, so the evidence is a reversion that fails a named case rather than a claim that the code looks right.

waitlist.rule: A full wait-list is not in scope. Disable waitlist_conversion as a selectable or claimable channel, report no wait-list conversion metrics, never claim a customer has joined a wait-list. A paused-city request stays an ordinary CRM lead or service-interest record.
waitlist.measured_before: waitlist_conversion was a first-class member of BOOKING_CHANNELS gated only by city status, so in a LIVE city it was ACCEPTED - a booking could arrive claiming to be a wait-list conversion when no wait-list has ever existed: no table, no module, no route, no join, no consent, no ordering.
waitlist.implemented: waitlistAvailable() is a single function returning false, so the day the feature lands there is exactly one line to change. SELECTABLE_BOOKING_CHANNELS excludes the channel. cityBookingVerdict refuses it with reason waitlist_not_available even in a fully open city. A source sweep pins that nothing publishes a wait-list conversion figure.
waitlist.why_the_name_survives: Deleting waitlist_conversion from BOOKING_CHANNELS would be the weaker fix: the day a wait-list is built its bookings would arrive as an UNRECOGNISED channel rather than as one the city gate already refuses.
waitlist.why_it_sits_after_the_city_gate: The city status is the outer question. A paused city must keep answering city_paused on every channel - a separate rule with its own tests - and this is the inner one. Sabotage C moves the check ahead of the city gate and fails WL-05, which is what pins the ordering.

regression.red_before: Wait-list: 3 of 6 failing. Terminal states: green on arrival, sabotage-verified (see below).
sabotage_verification: Boarding terminal guard removed -> both TS-01 cases red
Taxi safety-workflow guard removed -> both TS-03 cases red
revocation cancels in-progress work instead of opening a case -> TS-05 red
waitlistAvailable() flipped to true -> WL-01, WL-03, WL-04 red
waitlist refusal moved ahead of the city gate -> WL-05 red

still_open_and_not_claimed.waitlist_feature: Not built, deliberately. FIFO by city, service and original request time followed by customer availability confirmation is recorded as future backlog logic, not implemented.
still_open_and_not_claimed.refunded: The source guards also treat `refunded` as terminal. The approved rule names completed and cancelled; refunded is stricter and consistent, and is left as it stands.
